abstract: N6-isopentenyladenosine (i6A) and its derivative 2-methylthio-N6-isopentenyladenosine (ms2i6A) at position 37 are conserved modifications of cytosolic and mitochondrial tRNAs that typically contain the A36-A37-A38 motif. However, their distribution and function are poorly defined due to the lack of methods capable of distinguishing these closely related modifications. Here, we developed isopentenyl-tRNA sequencing (isopentenyl-tRNA-seq), an approach that simultaneously detects and discriminates i6A37 and ms2i6A37 at single-nucleotide resolution. Applying isopentenyl-tRNA-seq to twelve representative eukaryotes, we uncovered extensive species-specific diversity and dynamic regulation of these modifications. Unexpectedly, we identified i6A37 in tRNAs lacking the canonical A36-A37-A38 motif and detected both modifications in chloroplast tRNAs. Moreover, integrative analyses identifed conserved and lineage-specific pathways enriched in genes with high usage of codons decoded by i6A37-modified tRNAs. Together, this work establishes isopentenyl-tRNA-seq as a platform for high-resolution analysis of isopentenylated tRNA modifications and provides a framework for understanding their evolutionary distribution and potential functional roles in eukaryotes.
